Which choreographic approach specifically modifies traditional movement sequences so that individuals using wheelchairs can fully participate in the performance?

options: A) To sell expensive paintings to collectors
B) To strictly enforce classical art rules

sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the principle of 'Proportion' in visual art when drawing 'People in Places'. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Proportion refers to the comparative size relationship of parts to a whole within a composition. When drawing people in environments, correct proportion ensures the human figures appear accurately scaled relative to buildings or objects.

questions.question_text: How does observing and practicing traditional 'Arts of the People' (folk art) help students connect with regional cultural heritage? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Practicing folk art immerses students in regional aesthetics, indigenous materials, and historical narratives. It preserves ancient storytelling traditions, fostering a deep appreciation for the diverse grassroots cultural identities across India.

questions.question_text: Describe how complementary colors can be utilized in a 'Still Life in Colour' to create visual impact. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Complementary colors, positioned opposite each other on the color wheel, create high contrast when placed side-by-side. This visual tension makes the painted objects pop, adding vibrant energy and dimensional depth to the still life.

questions.question_text: What does the term 'Inclusivity' mean in the context of creating a modern dance presentation? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Inclusivity means designing choreography and stage spaces that welcome performers of all physical abilities and backgrounds, ensuring everyone has equitable access to participate, express themselves, and contribute to the artistic narrative.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to define a clear target audience when designing a 'Campaign for Art Awareness'? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Defining a target audience allows campaign organizers to tailor their visual messaging, tone, and choice of medium so it resonates effectively with specific demographic groups, maximizing the campaign's social impact and engagement.

questions.question_text: Draft a practical guide for organizing a community mural project ('Arts of the People') that involves local residents painting a public wall. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The guide must include selecting a publicly visible, legal wall space and hosting a collaborative brainstorming session with residents for the theme. Practical steps involve sketching the outline using grid scaling, assigning specific color-blocking tasks to community volunteers, and applying a final weatherproof sealant.

questions.question_text: Create a staging script block for an inclusive dance sequence where performers with and without mobility aids interact symmetrically. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The script must detail a circular formation where seated and standing dancers alternate. Actions should specify synchronized upper-body arm waves (Port de bras) passing continuously around the circle. The staging must ensure wide spatial gaps allowing wheelchairs to pivot seamlessly without breaking the visual symmetry.

questions.question_text: Write a step-by-step rendering plan to paint a spherical object (like an apple) in a 'Still Life in Colour' to achieve a 3D effect. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The plan requires mapping out a light source direction. Students must apply a base mid-tone, then blend darker, cooler hues along the curved core shadow. It must conclude with adding a warm, bright highlight on the apex and a subtle reflective light near the bottom edge.

sections.section_name: Section D - Applied Art Advocacy & Campaigns

questions.question_text: Design a multimedia 'Campaign for Art Awareness' aimed at promoting local handloom weavers. Describe the visual elements and community outreach methods. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The campaign will feature vibrant posters highlighting intricate weaving patterns paired with QR codes linking to short documentary videos of the weavers working. Community outreach includes setting up interactive pop-up looms in public squares where pedestrians can try weaving, bridging the gap between traditional artisans and the modern urban consumer.

questions.question_text: Propose an inclusive performing arts event that combines 'People in Places' observations with 'Innovation and Inclusivity.' Outline the event's core structure. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The event will be a site-specific performance in a local park. Students will choreograph movements mimicking everyday activities observed in that exact park. To ensure inclusivity, the performance will feature live audio descriptions for the visually impaired and sign language interpreters integrated directly into the dancers' movements, making the art accessible to all.
